event: 2025 Consumer Analyst Group of New York (CAGNY) Conference
rows: 2025 Consumer Analyst Group of New York (CAGNY) Conference
Inaugural CAGNY presentation; management positioned Celsius as a 'category disrupter' with premium zero-sugar functional beverage brands in a large/growing TAM.
Recapped FY2024: $1.36B revenue, 50.2% GM, $145M net income, $256M adj EBITDA; reached #9 LRB brand at $2.7B retail sales.
Dominant theme: newly announced Alani Nu acquisition framed as creating a leading better-for-you functional lifestyle platform with ~$2B combined pro-forma sales and ~16% energy share.
Three-pillar growth strategy: more people, more places, more often, underpinned by operational excellence.

CMO Watson emphasized brand-building over commodity positioning ('Live Fit'); cited 72% repeat-buyer households, 7M owned social followers, 3,000+ ambassadors; competitors saw household declines while Celsius expanded.

Energy category framed as going mainstream: gender/age-balanced; sugar-free surpassed sugary energy for the first time in 2024 (from ~39% of category in 2020) - a structural mix shift favoring Celsius's all-sugar-free portfolio.
Margin expansion via operational excellence: Nov 2024 Big Beverages vertical-integration acquisition, scrap reduction, aged-inventory removal, AI-driven sales/marketing ROI.
2025 'healthy HALO' marketing campaign to launch prior to summer beverage season.
Foodservice expansion: Subway up to 18,000 locations (with Pepsi), Jersey Mike's, Home Depot; Hydration line 'selling out' on Amazon.

CFO framed Alani Nu valuation as compelling (~12x synergized EBITDA, <3x revenue); ~1x modest net leverage; year-one cash EPS accretion; founders gave 8.7% stock with 2-year lock-up and consulting agreement.
Management tone confident, promotional, forward-leaning; only acknowledged near-term challenge implicit in prior night's reported softness.
Note: Q&A abbreviated due to time constraints - only one substantive question taken on the main stage.
Asked for more color on the assumptions behind expected EPS accretion from the Alani Nu deal - magnitude of accretion, and whether growth above Alani Nu's 2024 base is baked in.

CFO Langhans said detail would come at a dedicated post-close modeling call, but management assumes 'outsized growth' beyond what is expected within the energy category. Cash accretion reflects expected 2025 growth plus synergy capture, net of estimated interest costs, synergy costs, and the 8.7% dilutive stock issued. CEO Fieldly added significant leverage opportunities in supply chain (building on Big Beverages), raw materials, logistics, and the larger combined sales organization.
